extracted.intended_audience: students and teachers running a classroom Page-to-Stage poetry book project (elementary/middle school workshop)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and checklists for student teams to produce, design, proofread, market, and present a class poetry book (front/back matter, layout, cover, printing, event).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial responsibility for front/back matter and back cover copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Your group is responsible for writing and typing all of the front and back matter and back cover copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided templates; look at other books in the library for information and inspiration; everything written/typed should be proofread by the proofreading department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front Matter (components)
rubrics_metrics.description: Front Matter: Copyright Page; Table of Contents; Subtitle; Dedication; Foreword; Introduction; Epigraph(s); Acknowledgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production Manager is responsible for the Table of Contents. Make sure each listed front-matter item is completed and proofread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Back Matter (components)
rubrics_metrics.description: Back Matter: About the School; About the Students; Back Cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The “About the School” section may be pulled from existing copy on the school’s website or promo materials. Production Manager responsible for 'About the Students'. Proofread all back-matter copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Back cover copy / Blurb
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and prepare Back Cover copy and Blurb for the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use teacher guidance or existing school materials as needed; include a concise description that sells/represents the book; proofread before finalizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epigraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: If your book will have sections, you will need an epigraph to start off each section. If your book will not have sections, you will only need one epigraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select epigraphs that set tone/theme; editorial team to write/type them and ensure they are included in front matter or section openers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial checklist: completion & assignment tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an editorial checklist that records ITEM TO COMPLETE, WHO IS ASSIGNED TO DO THIS?, COMPLETED, PROOFREAD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the checklist to track front- and back-matter tasks; confirm proofreader sign-off before moving to production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading primary duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofreading team: go through entire manuscript and correct all errors; use a red pen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read 'Understanding How Grammar Works in Poetry'; review Proofreader’s Marks and Symbols; make sure manuscript is numbered; proofread all new work created by other teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading tasks (daily priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tasks: On flash drive — Type all new poems; Proofread all poems; Proofread other departments’ work; Optional: Input all corrections into the Word file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete tasks in order of priority. Ensure changes are saved on the production flash drive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical correctness checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofreading checks: Every poem has a title; All pages (except blanks) are numbered; Author names and titles are correct; No misspelled words; No missing words; All titles make sense; Periods and commas come before quotes; No extra spaces between words or letters; All poems make sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this checklist when proofreading; check both content and typographic conventions (punctuation placement, spacing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard proofreader’s marks and symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the provided symbols to indicate corrections (delete, close up, caret/insert, insert a space, let stand, new paragraph, spell out, set in CAPITALS/small capitals/lowercase/boldface, comma, apostrophe, period, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the sample marks and practice applying them; use consistent marking so production understands corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar in poetry: consistency over prescriptive rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Normal rules of grammar do not always apply in poetry; grammar depends on beat, meter, and rhythm — but you must show consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you choose to rhyme, rhyme completely; if you use fragmented sentences, use fragmented sentences consistently; if you use punctuation, use correct punctuation consistently throughout the poem. Consistency increases readability and conveys intended mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar in poetry: grammar affects mood and voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Grammar choices (e.g., 'run' vs 'he ran') determine tone and reader response; grammar helps guide the audience and establish mood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select grammar and syntax to support the poem’s intended effect; read other poets for style options and inspiration (PoetryAmerica.com). There is no single correct usage, but smoother pieces typically affect readers more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production manager responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Production Managers must manage all teams, ensure task completion, and save all files from each department on the flash drive in a folder named after the school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect printed copies of each department’s work; hand everything in to the teacher; 'Guard the flash drive with your life.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Production technical specifications to define
rubrics_metrics.description: Production must research and define: Trim size; Paper color; Paper weight; Cover thickness; ISBN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record these specs early so designers and printers know exact requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production checklist & deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: Production tasks include: compiling editorial items (copyright page, subtitle, dedication, foreword, introduction, epigraphs, acknowledgments), About the School, Back Cover, marketing items (book party plans, media alert), design items (cover template, photos, fonts), proofing and ensuring everything is on the flash drive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the production checklist to verify proofread status and that items are on the flash drive before printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing checklist & promotional tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketing tasks: Book party plans; Media alert for book launch; Type contact info for local media; Video blog (optional); Coordinate a group photo; Write a blog; Periodic Twitter posts; Create flyer to promote book launch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide on event date with teacher (at least two months ahead); have everything proofread; prepare a press release and media alert using sample templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book party planning and program flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan date/time/location, public vs invitation-only, cost, publicity plans, program schedule (sample timings for arrivals, welcome, readings, special guests, signings), decide food, funding, and program details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided sample program as a template; confirm dates with teacher; prepare a sample press release and contact info for media outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video production checklist for book event
rubrics_metrics.description: Video tasks: choose device (phone/tablet/camera); choose quiet location; decide who records and who interviews; do a test interview; ensure everyone projects and speaks loud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use suggested interviewer script/questions; interviewer should have respondents direct answers to interviewer (not the camera); record name spelling on camera.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design team tasks and research
rubrics_metrics.description: Design tasks: Read Guide to Book Cover Design; find four covers you like and explain choices; identify available graphics programs; use Image Selection Form; sketch/draw cover concepts; brainstorm cover concepts; decide book size; research/select photos; choose colors, title font, color and placement; choose interior font and layout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document image IDs and sources on the Image Selection Form; present multiple concepts and explain choices to the team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guide to book cover design: make the cover customer-centric
rubrics_metrics.description: The cover must be a selling tool: right colors, photos, and placement of text; make it distinctive and intriguing to the eye.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research widely (hundreds of covers), sketch ideas, and become familiar with elements of good cover design (color, images/photographs). Consider artwork vs photography depending on theme; use stock photos/clip art as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researching cover images (steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 1: Search photos related to theme/title on Google and stock sites; Step 2: Type keywords related to topic/theme; Step 3: When you find images you like, record the number or file name on the image selection form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep careful records of image IDs and sources to ensure proper licensing/attribution and to reproduce selected images accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing the right font for your book
rubrics_metrics.description: Serif fonts (e.g., Garamond, Bookman Old Style, Book Antiqua) are best for large blocks of printed text and should be used for main body text. Sans-serif fonts (e.g., Tahoma, Verdana, Arial, Trebuchet MS) are appropriate for titles, chapter titles, headers, footers and short lines but NOT for long body text in print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid Times New Roman for modern printed book body text; consider readability differences between screen and print; choose fonts that set mood and aid readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page layout principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Four basic principles for professional page layout: Contrast, Alignment, Repetition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contrasting fonts for headings and titles; choose one justification and stick to it (center for formal, left for professional, full for clean orderly look); create unity by repeating visual elements (ornaments, drop caps). Look at favorite books for inspiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interior layout decisions (mini-lesson questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide on headers/footers placement, text font, text point size, line spacing, and text alignment as part of selecting the book’s interior layout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should view and analyze other poetry book layouts, discuss likes/dislikes, experiment with layouts and then select a professional and appealing layout for their book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation self-evaluation: voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice-related elements: Speaks with a clear, confident voice; Enunciates clearly; Stresses key words for dramatic or humorous affect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect on clarity and emphasis; practice enunciation and intentional stress to enhance performance impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation self-evaluation: vocal control & pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrates strong vocal control, changing voice as needed to emphasize emotions; Emphasizes rhythm of piece; Pacing is just right; not too fast or slow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work on varying voice and maintaining the poem’s rhythm; adjust pacing for comprehension and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation self-evaluation: body and stance
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical elements: Plants feet and stands straight and tall; Relaxed and confident demeanor reflected in strong, steady stance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a confident physical presence to support vocal delivery; avoid distracting movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation self-evaluation: hands/gestures
rubrics_metrics.description: Manages hands gracefully (behind back, folded in front, at sides); Aligns gestures with voice to add emphasis; Uses gestures to dramatic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate gestures to reinforce, not distract from, the poem and voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation self-evaluation: facial expression & eye contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Makes eye contact with the audience; Relaxed confidence reflected on face; conveys 'true self'; Smiles when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use facial expressions and eye contact to connect with audience and convey authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation self-evaluation: overall presentation elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporates music, dramatic interpretation, movement, or props into presentation; Demonstrates confidence, passion, and conviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhance readings with appropriate multimedia or theatrical elements but ensure they support (not overshadow) the poem.
